title: Congruence
cover_sub: Same shape, same size, proved beyond doubt. Secure the four conditions, extend to proofs in quadrilaterals, then master proofs that use circles and isosceles triangles.

levels_long.s: SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS, and picking the right one.
levels_long.e: Proofs inside parallelograms, kites and isosceles triangles, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Multi-step proofs, and what congruence lets you conclude.

briefing: Two triangles are congruent if they are exactly the same shape and size. You only need to show one of four conditions: SSS (three sides), SAS (two sides and the angle between them), ASA (two angles and a corresponding side) or RHS (right angle, hypotenuse, side).
AAA is not enough: it proves similar, not congruent. A congruence proof is a short list of three facts, each with a reason, then the condition.
method: Name the two triangles, with the letters in matching order.
Find three pairs of equal sides or angles.
Give a reason for each: 'opposite sides of a parallelogram', 'common side', 'radii'.
State the condition (SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS), then what follows from it.

example.question: ABCD is a parallelogram. Prove that triangles ABC and CDA are congruent.
steps: AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal).
BC = DA (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal).
So triangles ABC and CDA are congruent (SSS).

s.blurb: The method, step by step. Show every line.

text: Write down the four conditions for two triangles to be congruent.
Triangle P has sides 5 cm and 7 cm with an angle of 40° between them. Triangle Q has the same. Which condition shows they are congruent?
Two triangles both have angles of 50°, 60° and 70°. Must they be congruent? Explain.
questions.answer: No: equal angles show they're similar, but one could be bigger.

text: In triangles ABC and DEF, AB = DE, BC = EF and AC = DF. State the condition, and name the angle equal to angle A.
Two right-angled triangles each have a hypotenuse of 10 cm and another side of 6 cm. Which condition shows they are congruent?

e.blurb: A step is hidden, or there's a context to unpick. One piece of tampered evidence.

text: ABCD is a parallelogram. Prove that angle ABC = angle CDA.
questions.answer: AB = CD and BC = DA (opposite sides of a parallelogram), AC common, so ABC ≅ CDA (SSS). Corresponding angles ABC and CDA are equal.
questions.tip: Once triangles are congruent, every matching side and angle is equal. That's how a proof gets you to the fact you want.

text: Triangle ABC has AB = AC. M is the midpoint of BC. Prove that triangles ABM and ACM are congruent, and explain why AM is perpendicular to BC.
questions.answer: AB = AC (given), BM = CM (M is the midpoint), AM common: SSS. So angles AMB and AMC are equal, and they add to 180°, so each is 90°.

text: ABCD is a kite with AB = AD and CB = CD. Prove that triangles ABC and ADC are congruent.
questions.answer: AB = AD, CB = CD (given), AC common: SSS.

text: ABCD is a square. E is on AB and F is on BC, with AE = BF. Prove that triangles DAE and ABF are congruent.
questions.answer: DA = AB (sides of a square), AE = BF (given), angle DAE = angle ABF = 90°: SAS.

text: Sam's proof is below. Find the flaw.
questions.answer: The 5 cm sides don't correspond: one is opposite 30°, the other opposite 60°. ASA needs a corresponding side.
questions.tampered:
Both triangles have angles 30°, 60°, 90° and a side of 5 cm.
So they are congruent (ASA).

m.blurb: No hints. Plan before you calculate.

text: PQRS is a parallelogram. X is on PQ and Y is on RS, with PX = RY. Prove that triangles PXS and RYQ are congruent.
questions.answer: PS = RQ (opposite sides), PX = RY (given), angle P = angle R (opposite angles of a parallelogram): SAS.

text: Prove that the diagonals of a parallelogram ABCD bisect each other. Let them meet at M.
questions.answer: AB = CD (opposite sides); angle MAB = angle MCD and angle MBA = angle MDC (alternate angles, AB ∥ DC). So ABM ≅ CDM (ASA), giving AM = CM and BM = DM.

text: A and B lie on a circle with centre O. M is the midpoint of the chord AB. Prove that OM is perpendicular to AB.
questions.answer: OA = OB (radii), AM = BM (M is the midpoint), OM common: SSS. So angles OMA and OMB are equal and add to 180°, so each is 90°.

text: ABC is isosceles with AB = AC. D is on AB and E is on AC, with BD = CE. Prove that BE = CD.
questions.answer: BD = CE (given), BC common, angle DBC = angle ECB (base angles of an isosceles triangle). So DBC ≅ ECB (SAS), and BE = CD.
questions.tip: Choose the triangles that contain the two lengths you need: BE is in triangle EBC, CD is in triangle DCB.

text: Explain why 'two sides and an angle that is not between them' (SSA) is not a condition for congruence.
questions.answer: Two different triangles can fit the same two sides and non-included angle (the ambiguous case), so they needn't be congruent.

closed_points: Use SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS, and know AAA isn't enough.
Match corresponding vertices when naming triangles.
Give a reason for every fact in a proof.
Use congruence to prove lengths and angles equal.
Prove properties of parallelograms, kites, isosceles triangles and circles.
